Anthropic Stock Is Back Above Its IPO Price: What Could Move Shares Next
Anthropic jumps 11% to $91.88, ending first full week above $83 IPO price
sum: - Anthropic closed at $91.88 on Nov. 27, up $9.09, or 10.98%, per Investing.com quote data; Yahoo Finance history shows the same close [2][3].
- Friday's range was $84.53 to $93.22 on volume of 143,747,654 shares, after an $84.99 open [3].
- The stock had closed below its $83 IPO price on Tuesday ($81.91) and Wednesday ($82.79), with a Wednesday low of $73.85 [3][4].
- CNBC and Sharecast put the gain at nearly 11% amid a broad rebound in AI stocks [1][5].

Anthropic shares jumped on Friday, Nov. 27, to end the company's first full week as a public company back above its IPO price. The stock closed at $91.88 in the holiday-shortened session, up $9.09, or 10.98%, from Wednesday's close, according to Investing.com quote data [2]. Yahoo Finance's price history shows the same close, an $84.99 open and a range of $84.53 to $93.22, with 143,747,654 shares traded [3].

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above an initial $70 to $78 range, and opened at $111.50 on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Nov. 19, Fox Business reported [4]. CNBC said on Friday the stock was up nearly 11% during a broad tech rally, after an earlier sell-off [1].

The table shows Yahoo Finance's daily prices for Anthropic's first full week and the day before it; markets were closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving [3]. The stock closed below its $83 offer price on Tuesday and again on Wednesday, when it fell as low as $73.85 after the open before rebounding to $82.79 [3]. Reuters noted Anthropic had briefly fallen below its IPO price this week as AI stocks were battered [5].

items.t: Anthropic Shares Close Above IPO Price After Two Sessions Below It
Anthropic Shares Surge 11% as AI Stocks Rally — A Sharp Reversal From Below IPO Price
sum: Shares of U.S. generative AI developer Anthropic closed at $91.88 on November 27, 2026, up 11% from the prior day — its largest gain since surging more than 17% above its IPO price on its November 19 Nasdaq debut. The stock traded as high as the $93 range intraday, its highest level since November 23, though it remained short of the $115.10 peak hit on its first trading day.

On Black Friday, the shortened session following Thanksgiving, investors rushed back into AI-related stocks that had been heavily sold off. The Nasdaq 100 rose 2.6%, the S&P 500 gained 1.6% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 1.2%, lifting the broader market. It marked only the third time Anthropic has posted a double-digit percentage gain since going public.

Anthropic listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT" on November 19. It closed its first day at $97.17, then fell to $88.91 on November 20 and $87.64 on November 23. It hit $81.91 on November 24 and $82.79 on November 25, both below the $83 offer price.

The November 27 close was about 10.7% above the offer price but still roughly 5.4% below the first-day close. Market participants say the stock is still searching for fair value after its post-debut spike and subsequent correction.
Roughly ¥18.8 Trillion Raised Through IPO and Private Placement

Anthropic announced on November 20 that, concurrent with completing its IPO process, it raised $26 billion (approximately ¥4.16 trillion) in a private placement to qualified institutional investors. According to documents filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on November 25, the placement consisted of non-voting Class N common stock sold at $83 per share, the same as the IPO price.
Seven semiconductor and IT companies participated in the placement: AMD, Nvidia, Google, Broadcom, Microsoft, Micron Technology and TSMC Partners, the investment subsidiary of TSMC.

Ark purchased 317,053 Anthropic shares across six ETFs. Seaport Research analyst Jay Goldberg maintained Neutral, highlighting a slowdown in quarter-over-quarter revenue growth to 44% in the third quarter from 144% in the second quarter.

Meanwhile, Wedbush analyst Ygal Arounian initiated coverage with Outperform and a $120 price target. Arounian highlighted Anthropic’s enterprise adoption and a potential market extending beyond traditional technology budgets into knowledge work, science and robotics.
According to Wedbush, Anthropic had more than 11,900 customers spending over $100,000, including approximately 1,900 spending more than $1 million.

Anthropic's Sharp Reversal: Up 4%, ANT Stock Reclaims $83 IPO Price After Early 8% Drop; CoreWeave Slides 2%, IREN Holds Steady
sum: This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

A sharp reversal has put Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) back on the right side of the line that matters most for a newly public stock. Anthropic stock is changing hands at $84.50 in afternoon trading, up 4%. That move lifts ANT shares back above the $83 IPO price after Anthropic first closed below that level on November 24.
Anthropic stock had dropped 8% before the rebound. The share price reached $75.71 during that slip. Even after the rebound, though, ANT stock is still lower than it was a week ago.

For a newly public stock, the offering price is the one cost basis every IPO buyer shares. Funds that received allocations paid it, so Anthropic’s first close below that mark left the whole IPO class underwater on paper. Recovering it may draw back buyers who read the break as a warning sign.

Anthropic’s rebound stands out against a rough environment for AI names. The technology sector’s slide reflects worries about the AI trade, and the NASDAQ 100 is nearing a bear market. Core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation for October came in at 3.3% year over year, above the 3.2% Yahoo Finance reported as expected. Traders see that reading as all but locking in a December rate hike from the Federal Reserve.

Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest bought Anthropic shares across its funds late on November 24. Wall Street’s first research calls on Anthropic also lean bullish, with Arete initiating at Buy with a $300 target, Oppenheimer at Outperform with a $150 target and Canaccord at Buy with a $135 target.

CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) stock is at $41.56, down 2%. The AI cloud provider had dropped 10% earlier in the day, so CoreWeave has trimmed a steep loss without turning positive. Year to date (YTD), CoreWeave stock is down 42%.

Anthropic Share Price Falls Below $83 IPO Price Within a Week of Record Nasdaq Listing; Stock Down 26.5% From Debut
sum: The Claude maker raised a record $93.5 billion through its public offering after underwriters exercised their option to purchase additional shares. Anthropic is scheduled to join MSCI's global standard indexes on November 30.

Anthropic shares closed 6.54% lower at $81.91 on the Nasdaq on Tuesday, November 24, falling below their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83 less than a week after the artificial intelligence (AI) company's record-breaking stock market debut.

Shares of the Claude maker, trading under the ticker ANT, opened at $83.40 on Tuesday against Monday's closing price of $87.64. The stock fell to an intraday low of $75.61, down nearly 14%, before recovering part of its losses towards the end of the session.

With Tuesday's decline, Anthropic shares have fallen 26.5% from their listing price of $111.50 on November 19. The stock is now trading 1.31% below its IPO price, leaving investors who received shares in the public offering with a notional loss of $1.09 per share. The company's market capitalisation stood at approximately $1.09 trillion at Tuesday's close.
The decline in Anthropic's share price comes amid renewed selling in AI-linked technology stocks on Wall Street.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.5% on Tuesday, while Nvidia shares declined 5.9%, reversing part of Monday's 31.5% rally following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive officer. CoreWeave shares also dropped 11.8%.
According to Reuters, concerns over elevated AI valuations, rising borrowing costs and substantial investments in computing infrastructure have weighed on investor sentiment towards the sector.

Anthropic shares plunge more than 8% below IPO price days after record Nasdaq debut
sum: Claude developer drops 8.3% to $80.34 in early US trading as Nvidia, AMD and other tech shares retreat

Shares of US artificial intelligence company Anthropic fell below their $83 initial public offering price on Tuesday, erasing their debut gains less than a week after the Claude developer began trading on the Nasdaq.

Anthropic fell 8.3% to $80.34 in early New York trading after closing Monday at $87.64. The stock was about 28% below the $111.50 price at which it opened on Nov. 19, when it began trading 34% above its IPO price.

The drop came as the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 1.8% in early trading. Nvidia slid 6.5%, giving back part of Monday’s rally after the chipmaker reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Advanced Micro Devices fell 10%, while SanDisk dropped 9.2%.

The offering generated a record $93.5 billion in gross proceeds after underwriters exercised their option to buy 147 million additional shares. Anthropic received about $91.6 billion before fees and expenses. The company also closed a separate $26 billion private placement with seven investors, including Google, Microsoft and Nvidia.
Anthropic disclosed in its prospectus that third-quarter revenue rose to $17 billion from $1.4 billion a year earlier, while its operating loss narrowed to $567 million from $3.1 billion.
Index provider MSCI said it will add Anthropic to the large-cap segment of its Global Standard Indexes after the Nov. 30 market close, effective Dec. 1.

She Flips $100,000 of Anthropic IPO Shares at the $111.50 Open for a $34,300 Gain. The Quick Sale Could Bar Her From Future IPOs and Makes $22,700 More of Her Social Security Taxable
sum: This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
She is 67 and single. Social Security pays her about $3,000 a month, and she takes $20,000 a year from her IRA. For years that mix kept her taxes low and her budget predictable.
Then her brokerage offered her shares in the Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) IPO. She put in $100,000 at the $83 offering price. The stock opened at $111.50, 34% above that price, and she sold right away.

That locked in a gain of about $34,300, and the timing looked smart. Shares fell 13% the day after the debut, and by Friday the Nasdaq had erased its 2026 gains. The quick sale still set off two consequences many retirees never see coming. One comes from her broker. The other comes from the way Social Security gets taxed.

Brokerages that hand out IPO shares at the offering price want customers who hold them. Fidelity can penalize buyers who sell within 15 days, and Robinhood (NASDAQ:HOOD | HOOD Price Prediction) and SoFi Technologies (NASDAQ:SOFI) use a 30-calendar-day window. Penalties run from several months without IPO access to more than a year for repeat offenders. At worst, a customer can be shut out of every future offering on that platform.

Access was hard to get in the first place. Fidelity required at least $25,000 in certain assets just to be considered, then ranked eligible customers by factors such as account size. Tax planning can’t win that seat back once she loses it.

items.t: Anthropic shares miss out on AI stocks rally, leaving IPO gains under pressure
sum: Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) shares were down over 2% in late-morning trading Monday in New York as the maker of Claude missed a broader rally in technology stocks.
The decline stood out among stocks tied to artificial intelligence, as Nvidia and other companies in the sector helped drive the market higher.
That left Anthropic trading about 6% above the $83 price investors paid in its initial public offering.
The stock had jumped 17% in its Thursday debut after the company raised a record amount in the offering.
Beyond the early swings in the stock, a longer-term question is how credit markets will absorb the company’s spending needs.
Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) has committed to spending about $900 billion on computing and infrastructure over the next two decades.
Investors expect major rating agencies to give the company’s debt a high-yield, or junk, rating, though no rating has been announced.

Why Did Anthropic’s Shares Drop 8.5% After Record IPO?
sum: Anthropic shares fell 8.5% on November 20 to close at $88.91. The decline came one day after the company completed the largest initial public offering in history.
It priced shares at $83 and raised roughly $81 billion in the base deal before underwriters exercised an option that lifted total proceeds to about $93.5 billion.
The stock opened near $111.50 on its Thursday debut and closed that session at $97.17. That marked a gain of 17% from the offer price. It reversed sharply the next day and traded as low as $83.05.
The decline came as early investors took profits after the stock’s strong first-day rise and as a broader sell-off swept through AI-related shares.
Concerns about high valuations and the sustainability of massive spending on AI infrastructure weighed on the sector, with major names such as Nvidia also falling sharply.
Anthropic, as a newly listed pure-play AI company trading at a rich multiple of sales, was particularly exposed to the shift in sentiment.

Profit-taking formed one of the first pressures on the shares. Some early investors who received allocations in the offering or bought during the first-day surge sold a portion of their holdings on Friday to lock in gains. That selling added supply at a moment when the initial excitement around the listing was already fading.

Anthropic IPO fails to prevent a tech stock wipeout
sum: Just like taking your high school sweetheart out to Dave and Buster’s wasn’t enough to save the relationship, Anthropic’s record $2 trillion IPO couldn’t reverse the unraveling of the AI trade. Tech stocks came crashing down yesterday—including shares of Anthropic, which plummeted 8.5%, at one point nearly hitting its IPO price of $83.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq nose-dived 5.6%, wiping out its gains for the year, while the S&P 500 dropped 3.7%, putting it in bear market territory.

Despite hopes that Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO signaled renewed investor appetite for the AI industry, jitters remain following Jensen Huang’s scandal-prompted resignation from Nvidia, which led to tightened US chip export controls.

Plus, many investors are skeptical about the costly AI infrastructure binge and worried that higher interest rates could temper borrowing by AI hyperscalers. And they anticipate regulation by newly elected Democrats when they take office in January that would slow the data center buildout:

Locking in gains? In recent weeks, institutional investors sold AI stocks, which analysts say is consistent with the common practice of taking profits before the end of the year. Investors appear to be rotating out of tech stocks into less risky sectors, propelling the S&P 500 consumer staples index up 0.68% and boosting government bonds.

Looking ahead…some analysts note that tech companies might be trading at a discount since their projected earnings are still strong, with the current price-to-expected-earnings ratio being the lowest since 2020, per FactSet. As for Anthropic, retail investors’ appetite for its shares will be clearer when its options start trading on Monday.—SK

sum: Anthropic's much-hyped arrival on Wall Street fizzled out on Friday, as a dramatic unraveling of the AI trade showed that even a blockbuster listing could not shake the gloom hanging over the sector.
Widely seen as a proxy for the AI trade, Anthropic's listing had been viewed as a potential boost for an industry struggling to regain its footing after a turbulent stretch.
But the stock was last trading at $88.24, about 9% below Thursday's close, while losses across other technology heavyweights suggested the IPO had done little to reverse the broader selloff.
"Investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth," said David Miller, chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds.
Among the Magnificent Seven stocks, Nvidia and Meta Platforms fell more than 3% each, while Amazon and Microsoft dropped 2% and 1%, respectively.
Chip stocks also slid, with AMD and SanDisk down more than 6% each, and Intel down more than 3%.
The focus now shifts to a potential OpenAI listing, which would be another major test of investors' appetite for AI stocks. OpenAI has indicated it may go public next year.

Technology company shares plunged after Anthropic's record IPO
sum: SoftBank, Samsung, SK Hynix and TSMC lost more than 5%, while Japan's and South Korea's indexes fell by nearly 5%. Anthropic's $81 billion IPO intensified the sell-off in AI company shares.

Technology company stocks in Asia fell on Friday, November 20. This happened after Anthropic’s record stock offering in New York shook the region’s stock markets and failed to offset losses from a sell-off in artificial intelligence companies’ shares. UNN reports, citing the Financial Times.
Shares in SoftBank, which owns approximately 13% of OpenAI’s shares, fell by more than 15%, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 index declined by nearly 5%.

In South Korea, shares of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, manufacturers of memory chips used in AI data centers, fell by more than 6%, sending the Kospi index down by approximately 5%. Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the world’s largest contract chipmaker, fell by more than 5%.
Taiwan’s benchmark stock index is heading for its worst week since 1991, having fallen by nearly 18% and lost more than $500 billion in market capitalization.
The decline came after Anthropic raised $81 billion in the world’s largest initial public offering (IPO).
Shares of the company behind the Claude AI chatbot closed 17 percent above the IPO price on Thursday, but the Nasdaq 100 index fell by 2.2 percent.

Anthropic Stock Jumps 17% in Record-Breaking IPO
sum: Shares of AI lab Anthropic ANT jumped on their first day of trading on Thursday, in one of the most hotly anticipated market debuts in years.
After pricing shares at $83 on Wednesday, Anthropic stock opened at $111.50 just before noon EST. Shares slid in afternoon trading and closed at $97.17, roughly 17% above the IPO price.

With its first-day pop, investors put the five-year-old company’s diluted market capitalization at more than $1.6 trillion, on par with Broadcom AVGO, America’s seventh most valuable company. Anthropic’s market value is about twice that of JPMorgan Chase JPM, America’s largest bank, and about half that of Alphabet GOOG/GOOGL.

The blockbuster listing is seen as a major test of the recently beleaguered AI trade. Tech stocks declined along with the broader market on Thursday. Shares of Advanced Micro Devices AMD slumped nearly 8%, while Nvidia NVDA and Broadcom declined 3% and 2%, respectively. Hyperscalers all closed in the red, led by Amazon AMZN, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms META, all of which dropped more than 3%. The Morningstar US Total Market Index fell about 2%.

Leading into Thursday, strategists debated whether Anthropic’s IPO would increase pressure on other stocks. “Today’s selloff is better explained by a switch away from the long-ingrained ‘buy the dip’ mentality to a ‘sell the news’ mindset,” says Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers. “Today was just the latest in a recent pattern of early, nascent rallies that morphed quickly into declines. To my mind, today was notable for the magnitude of the intraday moves, rather than the moves themselves.”

On Wednesday, Anthropic raised $81.34 billion in its upsized IPO, the largest in history. The company raised the number and price of shares offered after underwriters received orders for more than six times the 825 million it planned to sell. The company ultimately sold 980 million shares at $83 each, 12% above the midpoint of its target range.

Anthropic’s listing overtakes SpaceX’s SPCX June $75 billion offering as the world’s largest IPO. SpaceX’s total haul, before expenses, was about $86 billion after its underwriters exercised their option to buy additional shares. Anthropic is on track to gross much more.

items.t: Anthropic IPO: AI Giant Rallies As Tech Stocks Slide
Anthropic shares surge in New York in the biggest IPO on record
sum: NEW YORK (AP) — The artificial intelligence giant Anthropic opened for trading Thursday in the biggest public stock offering ever, despite investor fears of a possible AI bubble and public anxiety that the technology threatens lives and livelihoods.
Anthropic shares began trading at $111.50, spiking more than 30% above the initial public offering price.
The company priced its IPO at $83 per share, enough to value the entire business at $1.5 trillion, surpassing SpaceX as the largest IPO on record.

The price was surprising high given investor worries had ratcheted up even more recently following the stunning ouster of AI’s chief promoter, the CEO of Nvidia, amid a possible Chinese spying scandal. Anthropic had earlier set a much lower price range between $70 to $78 per share.
“It’s a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia,” said Dan Ives, a financial analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co. “The pricing shows strong demand among investors.”
A big test remains if investors maintain the classic “IPO pop” by keeping the stock aloft in its first day — or if it will tumble by the close.

Anthropic said it is offering 980 million shares to the public, mostly from the company but also from early investors and stockholders. The share price jettisons Anthropic ahead of SpaceX, which raised about $75 billion in June.
